cards.text: A father is talking to his son, and he leans in for the part that matters. "My son, do not lose sight of this: Preserve sound judgment and discernment." That's dad for HOLD ON TO THIS, I'm not saying it twice.

cards.question: The father tells his son to hold on to sound judgment and discernment. What does he say they'll be to his son's soul?

cards.text: He also calls them "adornment to your neck," so wisdom is jewelry now. FINALLY, a necklace that still shows up under a mustache like mine.

cards.question: With sound judgment and discernment, the father says his son's foot will still stumble now and then.
The father keeps going. When his son lies down at night, what does the father promise?

cards.text: And when he rests, his sleep will be sweet. Friend, I spent YEARS lying awake in the back of a junk drawer, so this one hits me right in the handle.
Then the father says, "Do not fear sudden danger or the ruin that overtakes the wicked," and he has a reason ready.

cards.question: The father tells his son not to fear sudden danger. Why not?

answers.text: The LORD will be his confidence
He will see it coming early
He is strong enough to face it

cards.text: The LORD will also "keep your foot from the snare." Then the father turns from his son's safety to how his son treats the people around him.

cards.question: The father says, "Do not withhold ___ from the deserving when it is within your power to act."
The father says it's fine to tell your neighbor to come back tomorrow, even when you already have the means to help today.

cards.text: "Come back tomorrow" when the help is already sitting RIGHT THERE? That's hitting the snooze button on your neighbor, and the father says NOPE.

cards.question: The father says, "Do not devise evil against your neighbor." What reason does he give?

answers.text: He trusts you and lives beside you
He might find out what you did
He could pay you back for it

cards.question: The father adds, "Do not accuse a man without ___, when he has done you no harm."

cards.text: Then the father points to a different kind of man: a violent one. Oh, my eyebrows just went UP.

cards.question: About the violent man, the father says, "Do not ___ a violent man or choose any of his ways."
The father explains that the LORD detests the perverse but is a friend to the upright.

cards.text: Now the father lines things up in pairs, like two cookies side by side on a tray. "The curse of the LORD is on the house of the wicked, but He blesses the home of the righteous."

cards.question: Next pair: the LORD mocks the mockers. In the other half of that pair, who does He give grace to?
The last pair: "The wise will inherit ___, but fools are held up to ___."

findings.problem: The passage starts in the middle of a thought. "Do not lose sight of this" points back to the wisdom just described in Proverbs 3:19-20, but the opening card never says what "this" is. The baker gets no context for the start.

rule.text: If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The card says "so wisdom is jewelry now." Verse 22 calls sound judgment and discernment the adornment to your neck. It doesn't call wisdom that.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question says "When his son lies down at night." Verse 24 says only "When you lie down," with no time given.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "He'll wake up rich" is silly and doesn't match the tone of the other answers. A baker can rule it out without thinking about the passage.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: "Oh, my eyebrows just went UP" is a filler reaction, not a real laugh. It reads like a nice dad being pleasant.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The baker has to guess the exact word of the line (envy, fear or judge). Card 15 gives no context to reason toward envy, and "Do not fear a violent man" or "Do not judge a violent man" would sound just as plausible. Right now it comes down to luck.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: This fill in the blank tests the exact wording of verse 31, not meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
